360	**Also found by this step's own Scorer (2026-09-19), not this step's to fix:** `product-quantity-picker.tsx` (Tier 2, in B3's manifest) now has zero real callers anywhere in the app. `product-item/index.tsx` dropped its import in step 3.5/commit `c426c4ef` when `ZimmQuantityStepper` was wired in to replace it as the real interactive control, and nothing else under `overrides/` ever imported it — confirmed via `grep -rn "from '\./product-quantity-picker'" overrides/`, which returns exactly one hit, the component's own `product-quantity-picker.test.tsx`. This makes the file's previously-cited live-region defect (reads the static `product.quantity` prop, never the live value) moot for the shopper-facing UI rather than fixed — nobody sees it fire at all anymore, correct or not, since nothing renders the component. Per Hard Rule #9 (never delete a file without being explicitly asked), this build leaves it mounted-but-uncalled rather than deleting it — same shape as the base `AddToCartModal`/`/cart` page pattern this epic already carries elsewhere (see HANDOFF.md's "Settled — do not reopen"). Flagged for Marcel to decide: delete outright (Tier 2, needs the same owner sign-off as any other Tier 2 change) or leave as-is.
361	
362	---
363	
364	### B4 — SFCC-250 + 272
365	
366	#### Step 4.1 — The merge call (must come first)
367	
368	**Consequence first.** Today, passwordless OTP sign-in from the wishlist auth drawer does **not** merge baskets. SLAS switches the session to the registered customer and the guest basket is **orphaned — the shopper's items are gone, not miscounted.** Until this is fixed, SFCC-250's AC5 has nothing to cap and SFCC-272's AC8 has no cart item left to move. It is step one of B4 by necessity, not by preference.
369	
370	**Mechanism.** Base `use-auth-modal.js` pairs its own passwordless flow with a `mergeBasket` call. `useWishlistAuthDrawer` reimplemented passwordless login for the drawer and did not carry the merge across. The social-IDP route is fine (it redirects through base `social-login-redirect`, which merges); create-account correctly skips (a new customer has no prior basket). Only `LoginPasswordlessUser` is affected. `grep -rn "mergeBasket" overrides/` is empty — no Zimmermann code merges anything.
371	
372	**Changes.** Add a Zimmermann-owned `mergeBasket` call in `overrides/app/hooks/useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`, with `productItemMergeMode: 'sum_quantities'` and `createDestinationBasket: true`.
373	
374	**Corrected 2026-09-19, before this step's Implementer was dispatched — the exact call site above was wrong, found by reading base's real mechanism instead of this paragraph's own original summary of it.** This originally said "at the point `loginPasswordless.mutateAsync` succeeds... around line 230" (i.e., inside `handleOtpVerification`). Base's own `use-auth-modal.js` does **not** call `handleMergeBasket` from its own equivalent of `handleOtpVerification` at all — it calls it from a separate `useEffect(() => {...}, [isRegistered])` that fires once the customer's registered state actually flips true, paired with `onLoginSuccess()`. `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts` already has the exact structural equivalent of that effect (its own `isRegistered` effect that calls `onClose()`/`onAuthSuccess?.()`) — the merge call belongs there, alongside `onAuthSuccess?.()`, not inside `handleOtpVerification`. Reasoning: `loginPasswordless.mutateAsync` resolving only means the SDK set the session; `isRegistered` (derived from `useCustomerType()`) is the signal that the rest of the customer-dependent state has actually caught up, which is presumably why base itself waits for it rather than firing merge directly off the raw mutation promise.
375	
376	Also corrected the same day: base additionally gates its own call on `hasBasketItem && prevAuthType === 'guest'` (via `useCustomerBaskets` + `usePrevious(customerType)`) — skip a pointless merge call when the guest basket is empty. This build deliberately does **not** replicate that guard (Marcel's call, 2026-09-19, asked directly): the `prevAuthType === 'guest'` half is already structurally guaranteed here for free — `handleTriggerClick` never opens this drawer at all when the customer is already registered, so every path that can reach the `isRegistered` effect's merge call started from a guest session by construction, with no `usePrevious` needed. The `hasBasketItem` half is deliberately skipped: replicating it would mean wiring a brand-new basket-loading dependency into a hook that has never needed one, on a step already flagged (pass criterion 4 below) as having no CODEOWNERS coverage to catch a subtle timing mistake — and the failure mode of getting that new dependency's timing wrong (merge silently skipped when it shouldn't be) is the exact "shopper's items are gone" bug this whole step exists to close. The failure mode of *not* having the check (one occasional harmless merge-call on an empty basket) is strictly cheaper. Call unconditionally inside the effect; no `useCustomerBaskets`, no `usePrevious`, no `customerType` needed.
377	
378	`sum_quantities`, not the SDK default `higher_quantity`, because AC5's "combined quantity exceeds the maximum" only works if quantities add. **This changes every merge, not just over-max ones** — a guest adds one dress, signs in a week later, the account already had it: today they get one, with summing they get two. Marcel accepted this explicitly. It must go in a comment on SFCC-250 (deferred to post-build) because no AC describes it and a tester finding it otherwise has no way to know two items is intended.
379	
380	**Pass criteria.**
381	1. `useWishlistAuthDrawer.test.tsx` asserts `mergeBasket` is called exactly once on passwordless success, with `productItemMergeMode: 'sum_quantities'` and `createDestinationBasket: true`.
382	2. It asserts `mergeBasket` is **not** called on the create-account route (base deliberately skips register).
383	3. It asserts the social-IDP route is untouched — no second merge added on top of base `social-login-redirect`'s.
384	4. **Regression gate on the other three consumers.** The hook is consumed by `header/rightBar`, `drawer-menu`, `product-view` and (new) the cart. Existing tests for all four still pass, and the PR body names all four as the change's blast radius. This is a shared hook with four call sites and **no CODEOWNERS entry** (see open question 3) — the review that would normally catch a mistake here is not automatically requested.
385	5. The hook's exported signature is **unchanged**. A signature change would need a team RFC (AGENTS.md "When to Stop").
386	6. Live verification is **deferred** per §7 — the code is in scope, the defect ticket and the live proof are not. Say so in the PR body so nobody reads the merge as verified.
387	
388	#### Step 4.2 — `useCartMergeAndCap`
389	
390	**Changes.** One shared function called by both the post-auth callback and the render guard — one implementation, not two copies.
391	
392	Settled shape, all of it: threshold **`>=`** not `==` (a line already holding 4 must fail the check, or the `+` stays live exactly when it matters); scope is **per line item**, not per SKU (the SKU is already size + colour, so in normal shopping one line is one SKU); cap **consolidates to one line at 3** (free — `sum_quantities` already produces a single merged line item); callback order **merge → cap → 272's wishlist resume** (the wishlist move acts on a line the merge may have just consolidated and the cap just reduced; reversing it moves a quantity the shopper never saw); render guard is a secondary backstop that **no-ops while `useIsMutating()` is non-zero**, so it cannot race the callback; **keep the loop guard** — one correction in flight, one attempt per basket version, then stop and surface an error, because a write-on-render without it can rate-limit a shopper out of their own basket; **no action on the brief 4-then-3 flash** — observe real behaviour first.
393	
394	**Pass criteria.**
395	1. Unit tests: line at 2 with max 3 → no change. Line at 3 → no change (`>=` boundary, the case `==` gets wrong is 4). Line at 4 → reduced to 3. Line at 5 → reduced to 3. Two lines of the same SKU at 2 each after a `sum_quantities` merge → one consolidated line at 3.
396	2. `useIsMutating()` non-zero → function returns without issuing a write. Asserted, not assumed.
397	3. Loop guard: two consecutive invocations against the **same** basket version issue exactly **one** write. A server rejection surfaces an error and does **not** retry indefinitely.
398	4. Callback order asserted: with all three armed, merge resolves before cap, and cap resolves before the wishlist resume. Assert on call order, not on final state — final state can look right with the wrong order.
399	5. Max value comes from `maxOrderQuantity.ts` (step 3.4), not a literal.
400	6. **State in the PR body that this is not end-to-end verifiable** until SFCC-268's `afterGET` hook is deployed (gate findings #1/#2 — the TSD is `v0.1 Draft`, Technical Lead sign-off Pending, and the live dev-sandbox probe found no `c_maxOrderQuantity` on any product, while Jira has 268 as Ready for SIT). The fallback path is what is being tested.
401	
402	#### Step 4.3 — `useCartMessages`: one handler, one file to swap
403	
404	**Changes.** Every message — success, error, warning — is emitted through **one** function, so SFCC-404 is later a renderer swap in a single file. A marker comment naming SFCC-404 sits at the emit site.

6. Live verification is **deferred** per §7 — the code is in scope, the defect ticket and the live proof are not. Say so in the PR body so nobody reads the merge as verified.

#### Step 4.2 — `useCartMergeAndCap`

**Changes.** One shared function called by both the post-auth callback and the render guard — one implementation, not two copies.

Settled shape, all of it: threshold **`>=`** not `==` (a line already holding 4 must fail the check, or the `+` stays live exactly when it matters); scope is **per line item**, not per SKU (the SKU is already size + colour, so in normal shopping one line is one SKU); cap **consolidates to one line at 3** (free — `sum_quantities` already produces a single merged line item); callback order **merge → cap → 272's wishlist resume** (the wishlist move acts on a line the merge may have just consolidated and the cap just reduced; reversing it moves a quantity the shopper never saw); render guard is a secondary backstop that **no-ops while `useIsMutating()` is non-zero**, so it cannot race the callback; **keep the loop guard** — one correction in flight, one attempt per basket version, then stop and surface an error, because a write-on-render without it can rate-limit a shopper out of their own basket; **no action on the brief 4-then-3 flash** — observe real behaviour first.

**Pass criteria.**
1. Unit tests: line at 2 with max 3 → no change. Line at 3 → no change (`>=` boundary, the case `==` gets wrong is 4). Line at 4 → reduced to 3. Line at 5 → reduced to 3. Two lines of the same SKU at 2 each after a `sum_quantities` merge → one consolidated line at 3.
2. `useIsMutating()` non-zero → function returns without issuing a write. Asserted, not assumed.
3. Loop guard: two consecutive invocations against the **same** basket version issue exactly **one** write. A server rejection surfaces an error and does **not** retry indefinitely.
4. Callback order asserted: with all three armed, merge resolves before cap, and cap resolves before the wishlist resume. Assert on call order, not on final state — final state can look right with the wrong order.
5. Max value comes from `maxOrderQuantity.ts` (step 3.4), not a literal.
6. **State in the PR body that this is not end-to-end verifiable** until SFCC-268's `afterGET` hook is deployed (gate findings #1/#2 — the TSD is `v0.1 Draft`, Technical Lead sign-off Pending, and the live dev-sandbox probe found no `c_maxOrderQuantity` on any product, while Jira has 268 as Ready for SIT). The fallback path is what is being tested.

**Changes.** Every message — success, error, warning — is emitted through **one** function, so SFCC-404 is later a renderer swap in a single file. A marker comment naming SFCC-404 sits at the emit site.

1	import { useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/react-query';
2	import type { ShopperBasketsV2Types } from 'commerce-sdk-isomorphic';
3	import { useShopperBasketsV2Mutation as useShopperBasketsMutation } from '@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react';
4	import { getMaxOrderQuantity } from 'app/utils/maxOrderQuantity';
5	
6	/**
7	 * The minimal basket shape this hook needs, regardless of which caller supplies it: the
8	 * post-auth callback (`useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`, wired in this step) passes the resolved value
9	 * of its own `mergeBasket` mutation directly; the cart drawer's render guard
10	 * (`overrides/app/pages/cart/cartDrawerContainer.tsx`, step 4.6 — not yet built) will pass its
11	 * own `useCurrentBasket()` data. `Pick`-narrowed, matching `cartItemMapper.ts`'s own established
12	 * pattern for taking an untyped-at-the-edges SDK response and narrowing it to only the fields a
13	 * pure function actually reads, rather than depending on the exact generic SDK response type
14	 * either caller's own mutation/query hook happens to produce.
15	 */
16	export type CartCapBasket = Pick<ShopperBasketsV2Types.Basket, 'basketId' | 'lastModified' | 'productItems'>;
17	
18	/**
19	 * Outcome of one `capBasketQuantities` call. A discriminated union (typescript.md's guidance for
20	 * variant/state modelling) rather than a boolean-plus-optional-error: each branch is something a
21	 * caller could reasonably want to react to differently, and no AC or copy exists yet for any of
22	 * them (that is `useCartMessages`, step 4.3, not built) — this file only reports what happened,
23	 * it does not decide what the shopper sees.
24	 */
25	export type CartCapResult =
26	  | { status: 'not-needed' }
27	  | { status: 'skipped'; reason: 'mutation-in-flight' | 'already-attempted-this-version' }
28	  | { status: 'corrected' }
29	  | { status: 'error'; error: unknown };
30	
31	/**
32	 * `getMaxOrderQuantity` is typed for a SCAPI product response (`id: string` required — see
33	 * `overrides/app/utils/maxOrderQuantity.ts`). A basket line item has no `id` field at all: only
34	 * `itemId`/`productId` (confirmed against the generated `BasketProductItem` type — verified via
35	 * a throwaway `tsc` repro that assigning a same-shaped object to a type requiring `id` fails
36	 * with "Property 'id' is missing"), so passing one directly does not type-check, despite it
37	 * carrying the same `{[key: string]: any}` catch-all a real `c_maxOrderQuantity` value would
38	 * arrive through once SFCC-268 ships. `product-item/index.tsx` already lives with the identical
39	 * gap at its own `getMaxOrderQuantity(product)` call site (`type SfccProduct = any`, lines 171
40	 * and 331) — narrowed here with an explicit, commented cast instead of a bare `any` parameter,
41	 * per typescript.md's "no `any` without an inline comment" rule.
42	 */
43	const getLineMaxOrderQuantity = (item: ShopperBasketsV2Types.BasketProductItem): number =>
44	  getMaxOrderQuantity(item as unknown as Parameters<typeof getMaxOrderQuantity>[0]);
45	
46	/**
47	 * A line needs correction once its quantity exceeds the cap — i.e. once it reaches the smallest
48	 * over-cap value (`max + 1`; `4` when `max` is `3`) or anything above it. Written as `quantity >
49	 * max` rather than comparing against a separately-named `max + 1` boundary, but the two are the
50	 * same comparison: this must be a "the whole range above the boundary" check, not an
51	 * exact-equality check against a single value — an equality check against `max + 1` alone would
52	 * correctly catch a line at 4 but wrongly leave a line at 5 or more uncorrected, which is
53	 * observably wrong against this hook's own test fixture (a line at 5 must reduce to 3, not stay
54	 * at 5).
55	 */
56	const needsQuantityCorrection = (
57	  item: ShopperBasketsV2Types.BasketProductItem,
58	): item is ShopperBasketsV2Types.BasketProductItem & { quantity: number } =>
59	  typeof item.quantity === 'number' && item.quantity > getLineMaxOrderQuantity(item);
60	
61	/**
62	 * SFCC baskets carry no explicit version counter. `basketId` + `lastModified` change together on
63	 * every write SFCC accepts (both real fields on the generated `Basket` type), so the pair is a
64	 * workable proxy for "the exact basket state a correction was last attempted against" — this is
65	 * this file's own reasoned choice, not sourced from an existing codebase precedent or doc.
66	 */
67	const getBasketVersionKey = (basket: CartCapBasket): string => `${basket.basketId ?? ''}:${basket.lastModified ?? ''}`;
68	
69	/**
70	 * Storage key for "which basket version has a correction already been attempted against."
71	 * Deliberately not a `useRef` — the post-auth callback (`useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`) and the
72	 * future render guard (step 4.6) each get their own separate `useCartMergeAndCap()` call, and
73	 * therefore their own separate refs, since they mount in two different React component trees. A
74	 * plain ref cannot coordinate between them. Piggybacking on the already-global `QueryClient` (the
75	 * same one `capBasketQuantities`'s own mutation-in-flight guard reads from — see that function's
76	 * own comment) via `getQueryData`/`setQueryData` gives real cross-instance-shared storage without
77	 * inventing a new module-level singleton or Context provider. It is also, unlike a React-render-
78	 * time hook value, live/imperative — reading and then
79	 * immediately writing it inside `capBasketQuantities` with no `await` in between (see that
80	 * function) leaves no window for two near-simultaneous calls to both pass the check before either
81	 * has recorded its attempt, since JavaScript runs that synchronous read-then-write as one
82	 * uninterruptible step.
83	 */
84	const CAP_ATTEMPT_QUERY_KEY = ['zimmCartMergeAndCap', 'attemptedBasketVersion'] as const;
85	
86	export type UseCartMergeAndCapReturn = {
87	  /**
88	   * Checks every basket line against `getMaxOrderQuantity` and, if any line exceeds its cap,
89	   * issues one `updateItemsInBasket` write reducing every over-cap line to its own max in a
90	   * single request (matching the SFCC-11 plan's "one write" framing even when more than one line
91	   * needs correcting). Resolves only once that write — if one was issued — has fully settled, so
92	   * a caller sequencing merge -> cap -> a future wishlist-resume can `await` this in turn without
93	   * racing it.
94	   */
95	  capBasketQuantities: (basket: CartCapBasket) => Promise<CartCapResult>;
96	};
97	
98	/**
99	 * Hook — the shared "cap" half of SFCC-250's merge-then-cap flow. Two callers share this one
100	 * implementation, not two copies: the post-auth callback inside `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`'s own
101	 * `isRegistered` effect (wired in this step, right after that effect's existing `mergeBasket`
102	 * call), and the cart drawer's render guard, which will live in
103	 * `overrides/app/pages/cart/cartDrawerContainer.tsx` (not yet built — a later step, 4.6, wires
104	 * that second call site; this hook is written to support it, not to assume it already exists).
105	 *
106	 * Per rules-of-hooks, call this at the top level of whichever hook or component needs it — never
107	 * from inside a `useEffect` callback — and invoke the returned `capBasketQuantities` function
108	 * itself from inside the effect/render path instead.
109	 *
110	 * @returns `capBasketQuantities`, the one function both callers invoke.
111	 */
112	export const useCartMergeAndCap = (): UseCartMergeAndCapReturn => {
113	  const queryClient = useQueryClient();
114	  const updateItemsInBasket = useShopperBasketsMutation('updateItemsInBasket');
115	
116	  const capBasketQuantities = async (basket: CartCapBasket): Promise<CartCapResult> => {
117	    // No-op while any mutation is in flight (this hook's own prior correction, the merge that
118	    // just ran, a shopper's manual quantity edit — anything) so this can never race a write
119	    // already under way. See this function's own JSDoc.
120	    //
121	    // REWORK (round 1, Tester-confirmed defect): this must be a LIVE read taken at the moment
122	    // this function actually runs — not a React-render-time value closed over at this hook's own
123	    // top level. `capBasketQuantities` is captured once by its caller and invoked later, from
124	    // inside an async callback (`useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`'s `mergeBasket.mutate(...).onSuccess`,
125	    // itself only reachable after a real network round trip) with no guarantee that hook instance
126	    // re-renders in between. A `useIsMutating()` value read at this hook's own top level (the
127	    // original approach here) would still reflect whatever mutation count existed at that earlier
128	    // render, not the real state at the moment this guard actually needs to check it.
129	    //
130	    // `queryClient.isMutating(filters?)` (confirmed against the installed
131	    // `@tanstack/query-core@4.43.0` source — a single deduped version across this project's whole
132	    // dependency tree, per `npm ls @tanstack/react-query` — `node_modules/@tanstack/query-core/
133	    // build/lib/queryClient.esm.js`: `isMutating(filters) { return this.mutationCache.findAll(
134	    // {...filters, fetching: true}).length; }`) computes this fresh from the live mutation cache
135	    // on every call. It is the exact same computation `useIsMutating()` itself wraps in
136	    // `useSyncExternalStore` for React reactivity (`node_modules/@tanstack/react-query/build/lib/
137	    // useIsMutating.esm.js`: `() => queryClient.isMutating(filters)`), just read directly instead
138	    // of through a render-synced subscription — so this preserves the exact same "every mutation
139	    // anywhere in the app" scope this guard has always had (commerce-sdk-react's basket mutation
140	    // hooks set no `mutationKey`, so an unscoped call is still the only reading that sees all of
141	    // them), it now just reads that scope live instead of stale.
142	    if (queryClient.isMutating() > 0) {
143	      return { status: 'skipped', reason: 'mutation-in-flight' };
144	    }
145	
146	    const correctedItems = (basket.productItems ?? []).filter(needsQuantityCorrection).map((item) => ({
147	      itemId: item.itemId,
148	      productId: item.productId,
149	      quantity: getLineMaxOrderQuantity(item),
150	    }));
151	
152	    if (correctedItems.length === 0) {
153	      return { status: 'not-needed' };
154	    }
155	
156	    if (!basket.basketId) {
157	      // No basketId means there is nothing valid to address a write at — surface this as an
158	      // error rather than silently doing nothing, so a caller can tell "nothing needed fixing"
159	      // apart from "something needed fixing and couldn't be".
160	      return { status: 'error', error: new Error('useCartMergeAndCap: basket is missing a basketId.') };
161	    }
162	
163	    const versionKey = getBasketVersionKey(basket);
164	    if (queryClient.getQueryData<string>(CAP_ATTEMPT_QUERY_KEY) === versionKey) {
165	      // Loop guard: a correction has already been attempted against this exact basket state,
166	      // whether it succeeded or failed — do not retry it. See CAP_ATTEMPT_QUERY_KEY's own
167	      // comment for why this is a live cache read rather than a per-instance ref, and why
168	      // setting it below, before the `await`, is what keeps this race-free.
169	      return { status: 'skipped', reason: 'already-attempted-this-version' };
170	    }
171	    queryClient.setQueryData(CAP_ATTEMPT_QUERY_KEY, versionKey);
172	
173	    try {
174	      await updateItemsInBasket.mutateAsync({
175	        parameters: { basketId: basket.basketId },
176	        body: correctedItems,
177	      });
178	      return { status: 'corrected' };
179	    } catch (error) {
180	      // Surfaced to the caller, not retried: the version is already marked attempted above, so a
181	      // later call against this same unchanged basket state returns 'skipped' rather than
182	      // hammering the server again — no retry storm.
183	      return { status: 'error', error };
184	    }
185	  };
186	
187	  return { capBasketQuantities };
188	};

| Conformance | PASS | Discriminated union for `CartCapResult` (typescript.md), narrow commented cast instead of bare `any` (`:31-44`), utility type (`Parameters<typeof getMaxOrderQuantity>[0]`) over a hand-rolled shape, JSDoc + `@returns` on the exported hook, hook filename/export match, no circular import (`maxOrderQuantity.ts` imports only an SDK type, checked directly). | Completeness | PASS | Both touched hooks have test coverage (`useCartMergeAndCap.test.ts` new, `useWishlistAuthDrawer.test.tsx` extended). No story owed — hooks aren't components (components.md's Storybook section only requires one for something exported under `components/`/`pages/`). |
| Restraint | PASS | Orchestrator verdict: IN SCOPE. Effort matches what the plan itself authorized — this is the one step in the 20-commit plan explicitly flagged for a mandatory adversarial pass, so the depth already spent here isn't an over-run. |

## What I tried to falsify

- **Reintroduced the exact bug class round 1 fixed, byte-for-byte, in the real file.** Backed up `useCartMergeAndCap.ts` (checksum recorded), edited it to capture `queryClient.isMutating()` into a variable at the hook's top level and read that stale variable inside `capBasketQuantities` instead of calling `queryClient.isMutating()` live — i.e. put back a render-time snapshot. Ran the suite: exactly one test failed, exactly the predicted way (`{status:'corrected'}` instead of `{status:'skipped', reason:'mutation-in-flight'}`), and it was exactly the test built for this scenario (`:193-216`) — the other 12 tests, including the sibling in-flight test with an intervening re-render, stayed green. Restored the file, confirmed the MD5 matched pre-mutation exactly, reran clean (13/13 green). This is a real kill-the-mutant result I produced myself, not a re-assertion of the Implementer's or Tester's claim.
- **Chased the "pre-existing lint violation" claim past a single git-blame.** Confirmed the blamed commit (`b16ebf619`, Jersey Perez, 2026-09-03) is an ancestor of `origin/develop` via `git merge-base --is-ancestor` (not just "looks old"). Then went one step further than what was reported to me: pulled develop's own untouched copy of the file into a scratch location and ran ESLint directly against it. Got the identical 3 findings — 1 `@typescript-eslint/unbound-method` error, 2 unused-eslint-disable-directive warnings, same rules — just at different line numbers (116/143/184 there vs 122/154/258 here, shifted by the new code this diff adds earlier in the file). This proves all three lint findings predate the diff, not just the one the Orchestrator named.
- **Checked whether the fixed bug class recurs elsewhere.** `grep -rn "useIsMutating\|useIsFetching" overrides/app` — the only hits are this file's own explanatory comments. The fix is contained; nothing else in the codebase shares this shape today.
- **Checked whether the open architectural dependency this hook was built against is still open.** `useCartMergeAndCap.ts`'s own doc comment names `cartDrawerContainer.tsx` (step 4.6) as its second intended caller. Plan.md confirms that step now exists (inserted 2026-09-20, today) rather than still sitting as an unresolved open question — so this hook isn't waiting on an undecided premise.

## What I could not verify

- **The true three-way order (merge → cap → wishlist resume) can't be proven end-to-end yet**, because the wishlist-resume leg (step 4.4/SFCC-272) doesn't exist as real code. The test at `useCartMergeAndCap.test.ts:265-325` proves the property that makes the real chain possible later (this function never resolves before its own write settles) using local stand-ins, and says so in its own comment. This is inherent to build sequencing, not a gap in this diff.
- **No commit message exists yet to check against verification-standard item 8** (no AI attribution, no third-person references) — this step is still uncommitted working-tree state (`git status`: 2 modified + 2 untracked, no new commit on top of `dcad4e90`). Check this at commit time, not something I can verify now.
- **Did not re-run the full 1646-test suite or the 4 named consumer suites** (`header/rightBar`, `drawer-menu`, `product-view`). Round 1 only touched `useCartMergeAndCap.ts`/test (confirmed via content-marker grep — the `REWORK (round 1` comment only appears in those two files); the consumer suites and `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`'s own wiring are unchanged since round 0, and were already reverified fresh immediately after round 1's fix. Re-running them against a diff that hasn't moved since is exactly the wasted-effort pattern I'm meant to avoid, not thoroughness.
- **Did not re-read the `@tanstack/query-core` source myself a third time** to re-confirm "dispatch fires before mutationFn, no self-vs-other distinction" — a prior pass already did this directly against the installed package, and my own mutation test above independently corroborates the same conclusion from the outside (behaviourally, not just by source-reading). Re-deriving the same unchanged fact from the same unchanged source a second time would be restating a conclusion, not testing one.

## Defects

None. Nothing here needs an instruction back to the Implementer.

## Biggest residual risk (since this is a PASS)

`queryClient.isMutating()` can't tell a basket-cap write apart from any other mutation anywhere in the app — it's deliberately unscoped (no `mutationKey` filter exists on any basket mutation hook today), and the code says so plainly in its own comment. Today that's harmless because this guard has exactly one live caller (the post-auth callback). The moment step 4.6 wires the second caller — the render guard, sitting inside a real cart page with wishlist toggles, quantity edits, and promo-code writes all able to fire around it — this same check starts getting exercised against real concurrent traffic for the first time. Nothing will double-write (that's proven), but a shopper's genuinely over-cap line could sit uncorrected longer than expected, purely because something unrelated on the page happened to be saving at that moment — not a bug, but worth watching specifically once 4.6 lands, since nothing today has actually exercised this guard under real concurrency.

## What Marcel is missing

Nothing new this pass on this step specifically — I looked for it three ways (grepped for the fixed bug-class recurring elsewhere: clean; checked whether this hook's stated second caller was still an open architectural question: it's resolved, step 4.6 already exists in plan.md as of today; checked commit-message hygiene: not yet applicable, nothing's committed). The one thing worth holding in mind for later, not now: this hook's page-wide mutation-blocking behaviour (see residual risk above) has never actually run against real concurrent app traffic, because its only wired caller today is the single post-auth callback — step 4.6 is the first moment that trade-off gets a real test, not this one.
